dokkai_a1_01.title: Reading: My Day
dokkai_a1_01.text: My name is Ana. I wake up at seven o'clock every morning. I eat bread and drink milk for breakfast. Then I walk to school with my friend, Budi. School starts at eight. In the afternoon, I play football with my brother. In the evening, I read a book and go to sleep at nine.

vocabularyList.meaning: to stop sleeping
the first meal of the day
the time after noon

questions.prompt: What time does Ana wake up?
questions.explanation: The text says: "I wake up at seven o'clock every morning."

questions.prompt: Who does Ana walk to school with?
questions.explanation: She walks to school with her friend, Budi.

questions.prompt: What does Ana do in the evening?
questions.explanation: In the evening she reads a book.

dokkai_a1_02.title: Reading: At the Market
dokkai_a1_02.text: Today I go to the market with my mother. There are many apples, oranges and bananas. The apples are red and very big. My mother buys five apples and two bananas. The price is cheap. We also buy some fish for dinner. After that, we go home and cook together.

vocabularyList.meaning: a place where people buy food
how much something costs

questions.prompt: Who goes to the market?
questions.explanation: The text says: "I go to the market with my mother."

questions.prompt: How many apples does the mother buy?
questions.explanation: She buys five apples.

questions.prompt: What do they cook for dinner?
questions.explanation: They buy fish for dinner and cook together.

dokkai_a2_01.title: Reading: A Weekend Trip
dokkai_a2_01.text: Last month, my friends and I went to a small village in the mountains. We took the train on Saturday morning, and the journey took three hours. The village was quiet and beautiful. We walked along the river and took many photos. In the evening, we ate dinner at a small restaurant. The food was delicious, but it was expensive. On Sunday, we visited an old temple before we returned home. It was a wonderful weekend, and we decided to go back next year.

vocabularyList.meaning: a trip from one place to another
a building for religious worship

questions.prompt: How did the group travel to the village?
questions.explanation: They took the train on Saturday morning.

questions.prompt: How long did the journey take?
questions.explanation: The journey took three hours.

questions.prompt: What did they decide at the end?
questions.explanation: They decided to go back next year.

dokkai_a2_02.title: Reading: Learning a New Skill
dokkai_a2_02.text: Last year I decided to learn how to swim. At first, I was afraid of the water, so I did not try very hard. My teacher, Mrs. Lee, was patient with me. She showed me how to move my arms and legs, and I practised every Tuesday and Thursday. After three months, I could swim across the pool. Now I swim every week, and I feel more confident in my body. I think anyone can learn if they are patient and do not give up.

vocabularyList.meaning: feeling fear
calm when waiting or when things are difficult

questions.prompt: Why did the writer not try very hard at first?
options: The writer was afraid of the water
questions.explanation: At first the writer was afraid of the water.

questions.prompt: How often did the writer practise?
questions.explanation: The writer practised every Tuesday and Thursday.

questions.prompt: What is the writer's main message?
questions.explanation: The writer thinks anyone can learn with patience and persistence.

dokkai_b1_01.title: Reading: Working from Home
dokkai_b1_01.text: Since the pandemic, many people have started working from home. Supporters say this saves time and money, because employees do not need to commute. It also gives workers more flexibility to organise their day. However, critics point out that it can be difficult to separate work from family life. Some people feel lonely without their colleagues, and communication can become less clear. Many companies now choose a hybrid model, where staff work from home on some days and from the office on others. This approach tries to combine the advantages of both systems.

vocabularyList.meaning: to travel regularly between home and work
the ability to change easily
a mix of two different things

questions.prompt: According to supporters, what is an advantage of working from home?
questions.explanation: Supporters say it saves time and money because there is no commute.

questions.prompt: What do critics say is difficult?
questions.explanation: Critics say it can be difficult to separate work from family life.

questions.prompt: What is a hybrid model?
questions.explanation: A hybrid model mixes working from home and from the office.

dokkai_b1_02.title: Reading: Protecting the Local Park
dokkai_b1_02.text: The local park has been a meeting place for families for more than fifty years. Recently, however, the park has started to suffer. Rubbish has been left on the grass, and several old trees have been damaged by storms. A group of residents has therefore formed a volunteer team. Every Saturday, they collect litter, plant new trees and organise activities for children. The city council has agreed to provide tools and money, which has helped the project grow. The residents hope that their efforts will encourage others to take responsibility for their community.

vocabularyList.meaning: people who live in a place
rubbish left in a public place
a group that runs a local area

questions.prompt: Why did the residents form a volunteer team?
questions.explanation: The park was suffering from litter and damaged trees.

questions.prompt: When does the volunteer team work?
questions.explanation: They work every Saturday.

questions.prompt: What did the city council do?
questions.explanation: The council agreed to provide tools and money.

dokkai_b2_01.title: Reading: The Role of Museums
dokkai_b2_01.text: Museums are often regarded as quiet repositories of the past, yet their purpose has changed considerably over the last century. Originally, many collections were assembled by wealthy individuals who wished to display their status. Today, most museums aim to educate and engage a broad public. Curators now design interactive exhibitions, and some institutions invite visitors to handle objects or contribute their own stories. Critics argue that this shift towards entertainment may compromise scholarly rigour. Nevertheless, supporters maintain that accessibility is essential, since a museum that nobody visits fails in its basic mission. The debate reflects a deeper question: whether museums should preserve knowledge for specialists or share it widely.

vocabularyList.meaning: a place where things are stored
a person who manages a museum collection
careful and strict attention to detail

questions.prompt: How did early museum collections usually begin?
options: With wealthy individuals displaying their status
questions.explanation: Early collections were assembled by wealthy individuals to display their status.

questions.prompt: What is the main criticism of interactive exhibitions?
questions.explanation: Critics argue that entertainment may compromise scholarly rigour.

questions.prompt: According to supporters, what is essential for a museum?
questions.explanation: Supporters say accessibility is essential.

dokkai_b2_02.title: Reading: The Urban Transport Debate
dokkai_b2_02.text: Cities around the world are struggling with traffic congestion, which not only wastes time but also contributes to air pollution. In response, many local governments have introduced low-emission zones and expanded cycling infrastructure. Proponents of these measures contend that they encourage healthier lifestyles and reduce long-term costs. Opponents, however, claim that restricting car use disproportionately affects workers who have no reliable alternative. They argue that public transport must be improved before private vehicles are discouraged. Experts generally agree that a combination of approaches is most effective, although they disagree about how quickly change should be implemented.

vocabularyList.meaning: too much traffic in one place
a person who supports an idea
to a greater or lesser degree than expected

questions.prompt: What problem do cities face according to the text?
questions.explanation: The text mentions congestion, time waste and air pollution.

questions.prompt: Why do opponents oppose restrictions on car use?
options: They affect workers with no reliable alternative
questions.explanation: Opponents say workers with no alternative are disproportionately affected.

questions.prompt: What do experts generally agree on?
options: A combination of approaches is most effective
questions.explanation: Experts agree that a combination of approaches works best.
